studies.Study: Lee JE et al. (2008) [PMID: 19033572] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Fat, protein, and meat consumption and renal cell cancer risk: a pooled analysis of 13 prospective studies.
studies.Title: Fat, protein, and meat consumption and renal cell cancer risk: a pooled analysis of 13 prospective studies.
studies.Authors: Lee JE, Spiegelman D, Hunter DJ, Albanes D, Bernstein L, van den Brandt PA, Buring JE, Cho E, English DR, Freudenheim JL, Giles GG, Graham S, Horn-Ross PL, Håkansson N, Leitzmann MF, Männistö S, McCullough ML, Miller AB, Parker AS, Rohan TE, Schatzkin A, Schouten LJ, Sweeney C, Willett WC, Wolk A, Zhang SM, Smith-Warner SA
studies.Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
studies.Population: Pooling Project of Prospective Studies of Diet and Cancer cohorts

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 1478 incident renal cell cancers (709 in women and 769 in men) were diagnosed among 530 469 women and 244 483 men during follow-up periods of up to 7–20 years across the 13 studies ( Table 1 ).

cases.excerpt: Intakes of neither animal protein nor plant protein were associated with the risk of renal cell cancer (eight studies included, n = 1019 cases).

design.excerpt: We conducted a pooled analysis of 13 prospective studies

timing.excerpt: and had follow-up times of up to 7–20 years to examine associations between meat, fat, and protein intakes and the risk of renal cell cancer.

ethnicity.excerpt: The Pooling Project of Prospective Studies of Diet and Cancer (referred to hereafter as the Pooling Project) is an international consortium of cohort studies whose goal is to analyze diet and cancer associations ( 19 ).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Each study assessed dietary intake at baseline using a validated FFQ or diet history.
exposure_measurement.location: Methods, Assessment of Dietary Intake, paragraph 1

gender.excerpt: A total of 1478 incident cases of renal cell cancer were identified (709 in women and 769 in men).

studies.Study: Maclure M et al. (1990) [PMID: 2090280] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: A case-control study of diet and risk of renal adenocarcinoma.
studies.Title: A case-control study of diet and risk of renal adenocarcinoma.
studies.Population: Incident and prevalent renal adenocarcinoma cases and neighborhood controls in Massachusetts
studies.comparison_type: Dietary animal protein intake, with and without energy adjustment (no quantitative contrast reported)

sample_size.excerpt: We examined dietary and other risk factors for renal adenocarcinoma in a case-control study of 203 incident and 207 prevalent cases and 605 neighborhood controls. Using unconditional logistic regression to control selection biases identified in an adjunct study, we found exposure odds ratios (OR) similar to those from other studies: 1.9 (with a 95% confidence interval (Cl) from 0.8 to 4.4) for smoking 2 packs of cigarettes per day; 3.8 (95% Cl: 0.78-18) for 3 or more packs per day; 1.7 (95% Cl: 0.9-3.2) for women and 1.7 (95% Cl: 1.1-2.8) for men in the highest quintile of relative weight (kg/m2); 2.0 (95% Cl: 1.3-3.1) for northeastern European ancestry; and 2.3 (95% Cl: 1.3-4.1) for history of kidney stones.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 203 + 207 + 605 = 1015

cases.excerpt: We examined dietary and other risk factors for renal adenocarcinoma in a case-control study of 203 incident and 207 prevalent cases and 605 neighborhood controls.
cases.location: abstract; cases derived from reported group counts 203 + 207 = 410
